messages:
maria (acme-prod): Hey team — our org `org_123` hit monthly refill at 00:00 UTC but for ~90s after the refill our API calls returned 429. Dashboard shows credits refreshed at 00:00. Region: eu-west-1. Example trace id: trace_abc123. Can you confirm why calls still got rate limited?

sam (support): Sorry about that, digging in. Can you paste a minimal repro (curl) and the response headers you saw? Also approx local time when this happened?

maria (acme-prod): Sure — happened right at midnight UTC. Curl: `curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer key_XXX" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate` Response: `HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests` headers included `x-request-id: req_20260317_0004` and `x-tenant-quota: 0/100000`. Screenshot of dashboard timestamp: https://acme.internal/screens/credits-midnight.png

sam (support): Thanks — escalating to eng. @jordan @lee can you look at tenant org_123, trace req_20260317_0004, possible stale quota after billing refill?

jordan (eng): looking now. Maria, can you also share the `x-request-id` from the 429 response body if present? Helps correlate to upstream logs.

maria (acme-prod): request id in body = `req_20260317_0004`. I uploaded a short HAR to the support ticket.

jordan (eng): quick find in logs: billing-service wrote new monthly bucket for org_123 at 2026-03-17T00:00:00.000Z. Event emitted to notifications queue immediately. However our quota-cache-service shows the cache entry for org_123 was last refreshed at 2026-03-17T00:00:45.000Z. Between 00:00:00 and 00:00:45 the cache still returned the pre-refill value (0). Snippet: ```[billing] 00:00:00.000 write success org_123 bucket=100000
[notifier] 00:00:00.010 queued invalidation event tenant=org_123 event_id=eid_998
[quota-cache] 00:00:45.012 cache-refresh ttl-expire check skipped tenant=org_123```

lee (sre): this looks like an async invalidation lag combined with a 60s safety TTL on the cache lookup path. If requests hit a cache node that hasn't processed the invalidation event yet, they'll see the old (exhausted) value and get 429s for a short window.

jordan (eng): correct. Repro pattern: billing write -> event -> eventual cache update. Race window is small (~30–90s) depending on queue fanout and node locality. We should have circuit that falls back to authoritative store when refill.timestamp > cache.timestamp but that's not happening in this code path.

sam (support): For now I can trigger an admin cache purge for org_123. Maria, would you mind retrying after I do that? Also we'll note this for an incident.

maria (acme-prod): please do — we have users blocked for a few minutes on scheduled jobs.

sam (support): done: billing-bot reports `cache-purge succeeded tenant=org_123 at 2026-03-17T00:02:05Z` :thumbsup: 

maria (acme-prod): retried just now — calls succeeded, no more 429s. Thanks! :relieved:

jordan (eng): follow-up actions: 1) implement synchronous small-window authoritative check when refill.timestamp > cache.timestamp, 2) add metric for invalidation lag per region, 3) switch to event fanout with ack so purge happens faster. I'll open an RFC/PR and tag as high-priority.

lee (sre): agreed. Also adding a short-term tweak: reduce cache safety TTL to 15s for billing-related keys to shrink the race window until the fix is shipped.

sam (support): Closing the support ticket after we confirm monitoring alerts and the PR. Maria — please re-open if this recurs. Thanks everyone for quick triage. :eyes:

maria (acme-prod): will do, thanks for the fast response!
